name: Inflammatory Linear Verrucous Epidermal Nevus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for ILVEN

criteria.description: Presence of linear, verrucous, erythematous plaques following Blaschko lines
Onset typically in infancy or early childhood
Histopathological findings showing psoriasiform hyperplasia with alternating orthokeratosis and parakeratosis
Chronic intense pruritus associated with lesions
Lesions often resistant to conventional therapies for psoriasis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of linear verrucous lesions with early onset plus characteristic histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Linear verrucous erythematous plaques following Blaschko lines
searchTerms: warty red skin lines following skin patterns
linear scaly red plaques along Blaschko lines
skin lesions in streaks following skin lines

pathognomonic.symptomName: Psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with alternating orthokeratosis and parakeratosis
searchTerms: skin with alternating thick and thin scales

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic intense pruritus localized to lesions

common.symptomName: Resistance to standard topical corticosteroid therapy
searchTerms: skin rash not improving with steroids

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or tenderness at lesion sites
Associated nail dystrophy adjacent to lesions

searchTerms: small swollen lymph nodes in area

rare.symptomName: Development of squamous cell carcinoma within lesions
searchTerms: squamous cell carcinoma in skin patches

laboratory: Histopathology showing psoriasiform hyperplasia with alternating orthokeratosis and parakeratosis
Negative fungal and bacterial cultures unless secondary infection present
imaging: Imaging generally not required; may be used to assess associated skeletal abnormalities
genetic: Somatic mosaicism suspected but no consistent germline mutation identified
other: Clinical distribution along Blaschko lines is a key diagnostic feature

distinguishingFeatures: Psoriasis lesions typically respond to corticosteroids
Histopathology shows uniform parakeratosis without alternating pattern

redFlags: Rapid lesion growth or ulceration suggesting malignant transformation
Secondary bacterial infection with systemic symptoms
Development of neurological or musculoskeletal abnormalities
references: Happle R. Inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal nevus (ILVEN): a review. Am J Med Genet. 1990;37(3):  371-376.
